description: We are Cosmorocco, a Moroccan team passionate about space exploration and technology. We bring together backgrounds in chemical engineering, and data analysis, with hands-on experience for teamwork and innovation
summary: Forgotten Footprints is an interactive website that gives a voice to the machines NASA has left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. For over 50 years, NASA has sent rovers, landers and probes whose stories remain buried in dense technical websites, so school-age space fans rarely meet them. Our solution lets users pick a world, open one of 14 retired machines and listen to its last transmission in the first person, supported by real NASA photos and verified mission facts. Each story links engineering (how the machine worked) to science (what we learned). The site runs in any browser with no installation. By turning silent hardware into stories, we inspire the next generation of explorers.
details:
What it does: Forgotten Footprints is a browser-based interactive experience about 14 retired NASA machines across three worlds: the Moon (Lunar Module descent stages, Lunar Roving Vehicles, ALSEP, Surveyor 3), Mars (Sojourner, Spirit & Opportunity, Viking, Phoenix & InSight, Ingenuity) and Deep Space (Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer, Kepler, Voyager 1).

How it works: Users pick a world, open a machine card and read a short first-person "last transmission", key engineering and science facts, and a real NASA photo (with a blueprint view for some missions). A "Next machine" button turns the visit into one continuous story, and a progress meter encourages users to meet all 14 machines.

Benefits and impact: It makes the history of NASA's retired missions accessible and engaging for school-age and casual space enthusiasts, and connects engineering (how it worked) with science (what we learned), inspiring future explorers.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript; no installation required, works in any browser.

Data: Mission details from NASA's NSSDCA catalog and NASA mission pages; photos and artist's concepts from the NASA Image and Video Library.

Creativity: Instead of a technical archive, each machine speaks in its own voice, turning silent hardware into a story.
